questions.questionText:
Statement: A school notice reads: 'Students must carry their ID cards every day.'
Assumptions:
I. The students have been issued ID cards.
II. Students dislike carrying ID cards.
Which of the following is implicit in the statement?
questions.explanation: An assumption is an unstated idea that must be true for the statement to make sense. Ideas that are too strong (all, always, definitely), predictive or unrelated are not assumptions. The order can be followed only if ID cards exist, so I is implicit. Students' dislike is not needed.
questions.shortcut: Ask whether the statement would make no sense if the assumption were false. Reject extreme words and future predictions.

II. Demand for seats increases as the train fills up.
Which of the following is implicit in the statement?
questions.explanation: An assumption is an unstated idea that must be true for the statement to make sense. Ideas that are too strong (all, always, definitely), predictive or unrelated are not assumptions. Both are implicit: higher fares earn more only if some still buy, and the design is based on rising demand.
questions.shortcut: Ask whether the statement would make no sense if the assumption were false. Reject extreme words and future predictions.
